name: Menor's Homestead Cabin and Country Store
summary: A tightly joined two-part hero cluster: Bill Menor's west/central cabin and the circa-1905 country-store east wing. The separate storehouse footprint is a registration anchor, not the country store; the ferry is explicitly excluded.

excluded.reason: The replica ferry and cable system require independent water-contact, current, cable, and thin-structure rules.
Menor's Storehouse is a separate storage/root-cellar building and must not be mistaken for the country-store wing. Its named footprint is used only as a site-registration anchor in this slice.
A separately documented building outside this cabin-and-store slice.
The current barn occupies only the approximate site of Menor's lost barn and is not part of this reconstruction.

placement.world_frame: x = easting - centerEasting; z = centerNorthing - northing
placement.strategy: Resolve the composite cabin/country-store geometry against the named Menor's Homestead footprint in terrain/public/buildings.json. Use the named Menor's Storehouse footprint as a second registration anchor to verify site orientation, scale, and topology against HABS WY-24. Never substitute the storehouse footprint for the attached shop.
resolution_steps: Record the buildings.json attribution, file hash, exact named feature rings, and world-frame origin used by the run.
Extract the site plan, plan dimensions, elevations, scale, and north arrow from HABS WY-24.
Fit the HABS cabin/store outline to the named Homestead footprint without independently stretching its three construction phases.
Check the fitted transform against the named Storehouse centroid and orientation; record residuals for both anchors.
Persist the approved cluster anchor, true-north rotation, component transforms, footprint hashes, residuals, and confidence.

budgets.material_policy: Share one compact whitewashed-timber, roof, trim, glass, and foundation family across the attached phases. A registered facade projection is permitted only on close-facing surfaces.

lods.intent: Preserve phase junctions, documentary openings, whitewashed timber character, and restrained foundation contact.
Preserve the three-phase stepped plan, joined roof silhouette, store/cabin distinction, and primary openings.
Preserve the composite outline, roof breaks, and broad whitewashed material field.

required_views.purpose: Joined cabin/store facade, whitewash, documentary openings, and phase continuity.
Country-store wing end elevation and roof/wall junction.
Legibility of the west, central, and east construction phases without changing measured geometry.

prompt_constraints: Preserve the exact registered target silhouette, roof topology, phase junctions, openings, crop, camera, and background mask.
Use only references proven to show Bill Menor's cabin and attached country-store wing.
Keep the country store attached to the east end of the cabin; do not replace it with the separate Menor's Storehouse.
Retain restrained lime whitewash with visible timber character; do not turn the building into clean modern painted siding.
Do not infer dimensions, roof pitch, openings, placement, or additions from image generation.
Do not add the ferry, cableworks, river, Maud Noble Cabin, barn, mountains, people, merchandise, signs, text, vehicles, featureless black rectangles, or baked cast shadows.
Keep tileable materials free of perspective, vegetation, sky, and directional sunlight.

checks: three LODs and exactly one active LOD
cluster triangle, draw-call, texture, and transfer budgets
projection registration at corners and openings
roof/wall seams and phase junctions at grazing angles
documented trees, paths, storehouse, and riverbank context remain intact
no production asset or manifest mutation

conditions: The cabin/store lacks the official HABS WY-24 identity and measured record.
There are fewer than two useful same-building exterior elevations for projection review.
Any acquired artifact lacks URL, author/creator, rights statement, retrieval date, and SHA-256.
A reference cannot distinguish the attached country store from the separate storehouse, Maud Noble Cabin, or replica ferry.
The named Menor's Homestead footprint cannot be reconciled with HABS WY-24 at confidence 0.90 or higher.
Primary center residual exceeds 2 metres, Storehouse anchor residual exceeds 3 metres, or orientation residual exceeds 5 degrees.
The country-store wing is placed on the separate Storehouse footprint.
The cabin-to-country-store relationship or three documented construction phases are not recognizable in every LOD.
Dimensions, roof topology, phase junctions, or openings are not traceable to HABS, LiDAR, the named footprint, or an explicit estimate.
Roofs intersect walls incorrectly, daylight gaps appear between joined phases, foundations float, or coplanar component faces flicker.
Projection edges drift from the approved orthographic targets.
Black placeholder openings, invented architecture, a baked landscape, or imagery of the wrong Menors Ferry structure is visible.
Vegetation or path clearing removes documented site context beyond physical building clearance.
Any cluster triangle, draw-call, deployed-texture, transfer-size, or LOD activation budget is exceeded.
The required High-quality capture set introduces runtime errors or regresses the agreed performance baseline.
